question: With per-product shapes (box dimensions, orientations) and height matching against the whole catalogue, does the lane stock estimator count box columns, keep refusing honestly, and not regress on cylinders?
decision_unit: one lane survey frame, scored on the lane it was taken for (stock_scorer, as CMB-114)

held_out_population.rule: the version-3 held-out seeds from box_seed_start (235) on, none recorded or read before: benchmark_perception splits v3 held_out >= 235
held_out_population.development_data: train and validation seeds >= 235 (37 seeds, 222 lanes, 89 box lanes) on which the estimator change was examined; no held-out seed was opened

noise_model: as lane_stock_acceptance_bounds_r2.json (Gaussian range noise 0.5/1/2 %, 2 % dropout, synthetic)

arms.abstain+degrade: half the frames lose a band of 30-70 % of rows
arms.not_run: oracle and channel arms: identity is untouched by this card

bounds.meaning: box lanes with sufficient coverage whose count is exactly right; a refusal is a miss (CMB-119: 0 of 3 right, 11 of 14 refused)
box lanes answered more than one product off, or a phantom
regression: every lane, cylinders and empties included
nothing wrong is answered under blinding
lanes still answered at 0.5 % and 1 % noise
empty lanes stay empty under noise

pass_rule: as lane_stock_acceptance_bounds_r2.json: a 'min' bound passes only if the lower 95 % Wilson limit is at or above the value, a 'max' bound only if the upper limit is at or below it, and the sample size is met; a bound with a 'group' is evaluated on that condition's block (a report with no such lane is inconclusive). Small bounds' samples reflect ~78 held-out lanes, ~30 of them box lanes; a bound that cannot be cleared by a perfect result at that n would be inconclusive, so the values were set with that in mind. A fail is recorded as a fail; nothing is re-run.
